title: SaucerSwap V2 CLMM on Hedera — residual unprivileged-value review
closed_reasons: Pool positions keyed by msg.sender: a stranger's pool.collect/burn on another's tick range returns 0 (PoC test_Pool_stranger_cannot_collect_others_position)

NFPM decreaseLiquidity/collect/burn are gated by isAuthorizedForToken reading the HTS LP-NFT owner; nft is set once by deployer (onlyOnce) and immutable -> no cross-collection tokenId confusion (PoC non-owner reverts 'not authorized')
pool.collectProtocol is onlyFactoryOwner; pool native HBAR leaves only to rentPayer via the owner (PoC revert + positive)

Periphery safeTransferFrom -> HTS transferToken with explicit sender: the Hedera network enforces an owner-granted spender allowance when sender != caller, so it is equivalent to ERC20 transferFrom, not an arbitrary-from drain (docs.hedera.com HSCS security model v2)
payer in MintCallbackData/SwapCallbackData is always the external caller; multicall uses delegatecall preserving msg.sender -> no victim-as-payer injection
increaseLiquidity/mint are permissionless (canonical) but only add liquidity
No EIP-1967 proxy on factory/NFPM/router/quoter (impl slot 0) -> not upgradeable
LP NFT has supplyKey = NFPM only and no admin/kyc/freeze/wipe/pause keys -> serials cannot desync and no privileged NFT manipulation
Faithful 0.7.6->0.8.12 port of UniV3 core/periphery; audit UVP-02M addDelta nullification re-checked as valid
key_facts: mintFee=500000000 tinycents (~$0.05/mint); poolCreateFee=1e16 tinycents (~$1,000,000) -> pool creation frozen (last pool 2026-07-06)
56 pools enumerated via mirror-node PoolCreated logs; measured 2-sided TVL $17,614,148 (DefiLlama $15,888,282); top pools HBARX/HBAR $7.46M, USDC/HBAR $4.15M
Pool native HBAR from mint fees = 2,132.29 HBAR = $171.82 (P-class, only factory owner via collectProtocol)
Periphery contracts (router/NFPM/quoter/factory) hold 0 HBAR and 0 tokens at read time
PoolAddress.POOL_INIT_CODE_HASH recomputation reproduces on-chain USDC/HBAR pool 0xc5b707348da504e9be1bd4e21525459830e7b11d -> deployed pool bytecode == verified source
No proxies (EIP-1967 impl slot 0); Omniscia core+periphery audits (2023) findings all closed/nullified; Halborn 2026 covers a different (Universal Router/Permit2/UniswapX) stack
caveats: PoC is local (non-forked): Hedera HTS/HAS precompiles 0x167/0x168 are system contracts with no EVM bytecode, so a --fork-url fork cannot execute token paths; allowance enforcement is argued from Hedera's documented security model, not reproduced in the mock
TVL is a point-in-time 2026-10-23 read; DefiLlama vs measured differ by HBARX (staked HBAR) double-count handling
Protocol-fee accrual across all 56 pools was spot-checked only (e.g. USDC/HBAR feeProtocol=6/6)
Latent (not E-U today): permissionless refundETH/unwrapWHBAR/sweepToken on router/NFPM take any balance left in those contracts; single-EOA factory owner can change fees/rentPayer and sweep pool HBAR
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live from SaucerSwap V2 (Hedera, $17.6M TVL): the CLMM is a faithful UniV3 fork, positions are msg.sender/NFT-owner keyed, collectProtocol is owner-only, and Hedera's network-enforced HTS allowances close the one arbitrary-from-looking path; only privileged surface is $171.82 of pool HBAR.
